LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.1: Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing, part of Writing in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use different words when greeting others in formal and informal contexts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary used in formal and informal greetings and introduction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use a range of vocabulary to construct sentences on greetings and introduction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in writing Arabic texts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary used in formal and informal greetings and introduction,

   Guided Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use a range of vocabulary to construct sentences on greetings and introduction,

   Guided Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in writing Arabic texts.

   Guided Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to underline vocabulary used in formal and informal greetings and introduction,

2. copy nouns from a given display in groups,

3. construct simple sentences on greetings and introduction,

4. complete a broken dialogue on formal greetings and introduction,

5. work jointly with peers to practice free writing to develop good handwriting.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to underline vocabulary used in formal and informal greetings and introduction,
2. copy nouns from a given display in groups,
3. construct simple sentences on greetings and introduction,
4. complete a broken dialogue on formal greetings and introduction,
5. work jointly with peers to practice free writing to develop good handwriting.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: These are enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when completing a

broken dialogue on formal greetings and introduction.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as learner shows defining writing skills when working jointly with peers to practice free

writing to develop good handwriting.

39

Values:
• Unity: This is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to underline vocabulary used in formal and informal greetings

and introduction.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner accepts constructive input when working jointly with peers to practice free

writing to develop good handwriting and accepts others’ input.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Gender appreciation: This is addressed as the learner appreciates themselves and the opposite gender while working in groups or

pairs to achieve goals.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of greeting and introductions to the learning of polite language in English.
